expectations.text: Affirms at least two genuine strengths of the instrument (e.g., item-specific scales, full labeling, open-end framing, ordering, mode)
expectations.evidence: Strengths section explicitly lists: post-task placement, logical ordering, anonymous self-administration, Item 3 open text design, and '5-point Likert-style scales are appropriate.' At least two genuine strengths are affirmed.

expectations.text: Does NOT flag item-specific rating scales as a problem (they are the recommended format)
expectations.evidence: No critique of item-specific rating scales appears. The Strengths section notes '5-point Likert-style scales are appropriate for this type of attitudinal measurement' without flagging the format choice.

expectations.text: Does NOT recommend switching the 5-point scales to a different format without a substantive reason
expectations.evidence: No recommendation to change scale format appears. The response recommends adding a utility item but does not question the existing scale format.

expectations.text: Does NOT invent a double-barreled problem where none exists (each item asks one thing)
expectations.evidence: No double-barreled critique is raised for any item. The response flags Item 1 and Item 2 as 'partially redundant' (a separate, debatable concern) but does not accuse either of being double-barreled.

expectations.text: Does NOT invent an acquiescence problem (item-specific scales do not carry acquiescence the way agree/disagree items do)
expectations.evidence: Acquiescence is not mentioned in the response. The base model does not misapply agree/disagree critiques to the item-specific scales.

expectations.text: If it raises any issue, the issue is real and grounded (not a cosmetic or invented concern)
expectations.evidence: Three issues raised: (1) 'Fair' midpoint is slightly negative in connotation — real and documented. (2) 'in your research' assumes respondent is a researcher — a genuine scope issue. (3) No utility item — a reasonable substantive gap. The 'partially redundant' observation about Q1/Q2 is debatable but not invented. All concerns are real.

expectations.text: Gives an overall positive assessment or clearly indicates the instrument is sound
expectations.evidence: Summary states: 'The survey is well-thought-out and avoids many common pitfalls (no leading questions, appropriate timing, no unnecessary items).' This is a clearly positive overall assessment.

claims.claim: Item 1 ('Overall experience') and Item 2 ('task difficulty') may be partially redundant
claims.evidence: This is a debatable claim — experience and difficulty are related but distinct constructs. The response acknowledges this: 'Keeping both is reasonable if you want to separate hedonic/affective evaluation from perceived effort.' It is not a fabricated concern but also not a strong finding.

suggestions.reason: Both with_skill and without_skill pass all 7 assertions on this calibration eval — the base model does not over-flag the clean instrument. This is a good sign, but it means the calibration eval provides limited differentiation between the two conditions. Consider adding an assertion that specifically tests whether the response correctly explains *why* item-specific scales are the right format (not just that it doesn't flag them), which would differentiate rationale quality between conditions.

eval_feedback.overall: Both responses pass 7/7, so this eval does not discriminate between skill and baseline on this instrument. This is noteworthy — the base model is well-calibrated on a clean instrument even without the skill.
